extracted.intended_audience: comedians, comedy writers, and performers who want to create or evaluate family-friendly / clean humor
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and standards for crafting stand-up or comedic material that is free of objectionable content and appropriate for specified 'clean' audience levels (e.g., club, TV, church, family). Includes content constraints, stylistic devices, and an evaluative checklist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absence of explicitly sexual content
rubrics_metrics.description: A comedy genre generally free of explicitly sexual content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit sexual references should be avoided entirely for many clean levels; at some levels (e.g., TV Clean) non-graphic mentions like 'we were having sex' may be acceptable but no specific imagery (genitalia, fluids, positions) or graphic detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absence of profanity
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Profanity is generally banned across 'clean' registers; TV Clean specifically notes 'no profanity'. Maintain language appropriate to the chosen clean level.

rubrics_metrics.name: No politically or racially controversial jokes
rubrics_metrics.description: A comedy genre generally free of politically or racially controversial jokes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid material that targets political positions, racial groups, or that could be perceived as inflammatory or discriminatory; choose universal/relatable topics instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: No toilet humor
rubrics_metrics.description: A comedy genre generally free of toilet humor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jokes involving bodily functions, bathroom topics, or similar lowbrow physical/explicit content are off-limits for clean comedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid similarly objectionable material
rubrics_metrics.description: A comedy genre generally free of similarly objectionable material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This catch-all encompasses other potentially offensive content (extreme vulgarity, graphic violence, explicit sexual metaphors). If in doubt, err on the side of family-appropriateness for the target level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Club Clean (PG-13) standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Club Clean (PG-13): General clean comedy for adult audiences; some adult themes acceptable; no graphic sexual references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material can address adult topics at a higher level of nuance without graphic detail; ensure language and imagery remain non-graphic and avoid profanity depending on audience expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: TV Clean (Edited PG-13) standards
rubrics_metrics.description: TV Clean (Edited PG-13): Sex jokes possible — 'we were having sex' OK — but no specific imagery (genitalia, fluids, positions). No profanity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allowed content may include non-descriptive mentions of adult situations; exclude descriptive sexual imagery and all profanity to meet broadcast/edited-PG standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Church Clean (PG) standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Church Clean (PG): Stricter — not all PG-13 topics acceptable; respects religious sensitivities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid topics that could offend religious audiences; focus on wholesome or benign subjects and respect community norms when performing in faith-based venues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Squeaky Clean (G) standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Squeaky Clean (G): Disney/Nickelodeon level — no edge whatsoever; family jokes, animal jokes, pun comedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material should be fully child- and family-appropriate: no adult themes, no edge, use gentle humor like puns, animals, and benign observational bits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rely on wit, structure, and craft rather than shock
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the joke rely on wit/structure rather than shock? (explicit checklist item)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because shock, profanity, and explicit content are restricted, clean comedy must use tighter structure, stronger setups and payoffs, misdirection, and crafted punchlines. The page notes that clean comedy 'forces deeper craft' and 'requires more material refinement.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Use universal themes and shared experiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful clean comedy draws on universal themes and shared experiences (parenting, work, relationships).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select topics with broad resonance to maximize relatability across ages and sensibilities; avoid niche references that require risqué context to be funny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employ wordplay
rubrics_metrics.description: Wordplay is a fundamental device for clean comedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Puns, double-meanings, and clever phrasing can replace shock value; craft sentences to reveal surprising interpretations that are family-friendly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use self-deprecation appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-deprecation is a recommended device in clean comedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poke fun at oneself rather than others; this reduces risk of offense while providing a vehicle for relatable humor in a clean register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use visual and situational comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Visual / situational comedy are effective modes in clean material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physicality, facial expressions, and well-constructed scenarios can generate laughs without relying on explicit content; stagecraft and timing are important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comedian persona consistency with clean register
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the comedian's persona consistent with clean register? (explicit checklist item)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The performer should inhabit a persona whose boundaries align with the chosen clean level — inconsistent persona (e.g., an edgy act that occasionally censors itself) undermines credibility and audience expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic appropriateness for the target level
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the topic family-appropriate at the target level? (explicit checklist item)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate each joke against the specific level's constraints (Club, TV, Church, Squeaky Clean). A topic acceptable at Club Clean may be inappropriate for Church Clean or Squeaky Clean.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the joke land at the target audience's 'clean' level?
rubrics_metrics.description: Could the joke land at the target audience's 'clean' level? (explicit checklist item)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider audience expectations and sensibilities — measure potential punchline interpretation, double meanings, and implied content to ensure the joke will register as funny without crossing the clean threshold.
